meta.act: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — First Schedule (Orders)

items.head: Who may be joined as plaintiffs
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: Persons may join as plaintiffs where the right to relief arises from the same act or transaction and a common question of law or fact would arise.

items.head: Who may be joined as defendants
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: Persons may be joined as defendants where the right to relief against them arises from the same act or transaction and a common question of law or fact would arise.

items.head: Representative suit
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: Where many persons have the same interest, one or more may sue or be sued on behalf of all, with the court's permission and notice to all interested persons.

items.head: Misjoinder and non-joinder
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: No suit fails only because of misjoinder or non-joinder of parties — except non-joinder of a necessary party.

items.head: Striking out, adding or substituting parties
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: At any stage the court may strike out a party improperly joined or add any person whose presence is needed to settle all questions in the suit.

items.head: Objections as to parties
items.group: Order I — Parties of suits
items.gist: Objections of non-joinder or misjoinder must be taken at the earliest opportunity, otherwise they are treated as waived.

items.head: Frame of suit
items.group: Order II — Frame of suit
items.gist: Every suit should, as far as practicable, be framed so as to give ground for a final decision on the matters in dispute and prevent further litigation.

items.head: Suit to include the whole claim
items.group: Order II — Frame of suit
items.gist: A plaintiff must claim everything he is entitled to on a cause of action. A part omitted or a relief omitted without the court's leave cannot be sued for later.

items.head: Joinder of causes of action
items.group: Order II — Frame of suit
items.gist: A plaintiff may unite several causes of action against the same defendant(s) in one suit.

items.head: Only certain claims with recovery of immovable property
items.group: Order II — Frame of suit
items.gist: A suit for recovery of immovable property may join only claims for mesne profits, damages for breach of contract under which the property is held, and claims for the same cause of action — unless the court allows otherwise.

items.head: Appearance in person, by agent or pleader
items.group: Order III — Recognised agents and pleaders
items.gist: A party may appear or act in person, through a recognised agent, or through a pleader.

items.head: Recognised agents
items.group: Order III — Recognised agents and pleaders
items.gist: Recognised agents include persons holding a power of attorney authorising them to appear and act for the party.

items.head: Appointment of pleader
items.group: Order III — Recognised agents and pleaders
items.gist: A pleader is appointed by a document in writing signed by the party (the vakalatnama), filed in court.

items.head: Suit instituted by plaint
items.group: Order IV — Institution of suits
items.gist: Every suit is instituted by presenting a plaint in duplicate to the court or an officer appointed for that purpose. A plaint that does not comply with Orders VI and VII is not duly instituted.

items.head: Register of suits
items.group: Order IV — Institution of suits
items.gist: The court enters particulars of every suit in a register of civil suits, numbered in the order in which plaints are presented.

items.head: Summons
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: When a suit is duly instituted, summons issue to the defendant to appear and file a written statement within 30 days of service.

items.head: Copy of plaint annexed
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: Every summons is accompanied by a copy of the plaint.

items.head: Delivery of summons by court
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: Summons may be served by the court's officer, by registered post, by approved courier, fax or e-mail.

items.head: Personal service
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: Wherever practicable, summons are served on the defendant in person or on his authorised agent.

items.head: Service on adult family member
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: If the defendant is absent and not likely to return in reasonable time, summons may be served on an adult member of his family residing with him (not a servant).

items.head: Affixing when service refused
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: If the defendant refuses to accept service or cannot be found, the serving officer may affix a copy on the outer door or a conspicuous part of the house.

items.head: Substituted service
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: Where the court is satisfied the defendant is avoiding service or cannot be served in the ordinary way, it may order substituted service — affixing in court and at the house, or advertisement in a newspaper.

items.head: Defendant residing outside India
items.group: Order V — Issue and service of summons
items.gist: Where the defendant lives outside India with no agent in India, summons may be sent by post, courier, fax or e-mail.

items.head: Pleading
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: 'Pleading' means a plaint or a written statement.

items.head: Material facts only
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: Pleadings state material facts only — not the evidence by which they are to be proved, and not law — concisely, in numbered paragraphs.

items.head: Particulars to be given
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: Where a party relies on misrepresentation, fraud, breach of trust, wilful default or undue influence, full particulars must be stated.

items.head: Signing
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: Every pleading is signed by the party and by his pleader, if any.

items.head: Verification
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: Every pleading is verified by the party, stating which paragraphs are true to his own knowledge and which on information believed to be true.

items.head: Striking out pleadings
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: The court may strike out any matter in a pleading that is unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous or vexatious, tends to delay a fair trial, or is an abuse of process.

items.head: Amendment of pleadings
items.group: Order VI — Pleadings generally
items.gist: The court may allow amendment at any stage if necessary to decide the real question in controversy. After the trial has begun, only if the party could not have raised the matter earlier despite due diligence.

items.head: Particulars of plaint
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: A plaint states: the court; name and residence of plaintiff and defendant; facts of the cause of action and when it arose; facts showing jurisdiction; the relief claimed; any set-off allowed; and the value of the subject-matter for jurisdiction and court-fee.

items.head: Money suits
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: In a suit for money, the plaint states the precise amount claimed.

items.head: Immovable property
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: Where the subject-matter is immovable property, the plaint describes it well enough to identify it (boundaries, survey numbers).

items.head: Relief to be specifically stated
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: The plaint must specifically state the relief claimed, simply or in the alternative.

items.head: Return of plaint
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: At any stage the court returns the plaint to be presented to the proper court if it lacks jurisdiction.

items.head: Appearance in the proper court
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: When returning a plaint after the defendant has appeared, the court may fix a date for appearance in the proper court.

items.head: Rejection of plaint
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: The plaint is rejected where it discloses no cause of action; relief is undervalued and not corrected in time; it is insufficiently stamped and not made good; the suit appears barred by any law; it is not filed in duplicate; or r.9 is not complied with.

items.head: Fresh plaint after rejection
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: Rejection of a plaint does not by itself stop the plaintiff from presenting a fresh plaint on the same cause of action.

items.head: Documents relied on
items.group: Order VII — Plaint
items.gist: Documents the plaintiff sues upon or relies on must be listed and produced with the plaint. A document not so produced cannot be received in evidence later without the court's leave.

items.head: Written statement
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: The defendant files a written statement within 30 days of service of summons. The court may extend this to not more than 90 days for recorded reasons. (Commercial suits: 120 days, strictly.)

items.head: Documents relied on by defendant
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: The defendant lists and produces the documents on which he bases his defence or claim with the written statement.

items.head: New facts specially pleaded
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: The defendant must raise all matters showing the suit is not maintainable or the transaction is void or voidable, and any new fact that would take the plaintiff by surprise.

items.head: Denial to be specific
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: A general denial is not enough; each allegation of fact not admitted must be denied specifically.

items.head: Evasive denial
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: Denials must not be evasive; they must answer the point of substance.

items.head: Specific denial
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: An allegation of fact not denied specifically or by necessary implication is taken as admitted (except against a person under disability).

items.head: Particulars of set-off
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: In a suit for money, the defendant may claim set-off of an ascertained sum legally recoverable from the plaintiff, within the court's pecuniary jurisdiction. It has the effect of a cross-suit.

items.head: Counter-claim
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: The defendant may set up a counter-claim on any right or claim accruing before or after the suit but before his defence is delivered, within the court's pecuniary limits. It is treated as a plaint (rr.6A–6G).

items.head: Subsequent pleadings
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: No pleading after the written statement (other than by way of defence to a counter-claim) is allowed except with the court's leave.

items.head: Failure to file written statement
items.group: Order VIII — Written statement, set-off and counter-claim
items.gist: If the defendant fails to file the written statement in time, the court may pronounce judgment against him or pass such order as it thinks fit.

items.head: Parties to appear
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: On the day fixed in the summons, the parties appear in person or by pleader, and the suit is heard unless adjourned.

items.head: Neither party appears
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: If neither party appears when the suit is called, the court may dismiss it.

items.head: Fresh suit or restoration
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: After dismissal under r.2 or r.3, the plaintiff may bring a fresh suit (subject to limitation) or apply to set aside the dismissal for sufficient cause.

items.head: Only plaintiff appears
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: If the plaintiff appears and the defendant does not, and the summons was duly served, the court may hear the suit ex parte.

items.head: Defendant shows cause before decree
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: A defendant who was proceeded against ex parte may be heard on an adjourned date if he shows good cause for his earlier absence.

items.head: Only defendant appears
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: If the defendant appears and the plaintiff does not, the court dismisses the suit — unless the defendant admits the claim or part of it, in which case decree passes on the admission.

items.head: Bar to fresh suit
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: A plaintiff whose suit is wholly or partly dismissed under r.8 cannot bring a fresh suit on the same cause of action, but may apply to set aside the dismissal for sufficient cause.

items.head: Setting aside ex parte decree
items.group: Order IX — Appearance of parties and consequence of non-appearance
items.gist: The defendant may apply to set aside an ex parte decree if summons was not duly served, or he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing. Mere irregularity in service is not enough if he had notice in time.

items.head: Ascertain admissions and denials
items.group: Order X — Examination of parties by the court
items.gist: At the first hearing the court asks each party whether he admits or denies the allegations of fact in the other's pleading, and records it.

items.head: Direction to opt for ADR
items.group: Order X — Examination of parties by the court
items.gist: After recording admissions and denials, the court directs the parties to opt for a mode of settlement outside court under S.89 — arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement including Lok Adalat, or mediation.

items.head: Oral examination
items.group: Order X — Examination of parties by the court
items.gist: The court may orally examine a party, or a person accompanying him, to clarify matters in controversy.

items.head: Interrogatories
items.group: Order XI — Discovery and inspection
items.gist: With the court's leave, a party may deliver written questions (interrogatories) to the other side, to be answered on affidavit.

items.head: Discovery of documents
items.group: Order XI — Discovery and inspection
items.gist: A party may apply for an order directing the other party to disclose on oath the documents in his possession relating to the matter in question.

items.head: Inspection of documents
items.group: Order XI — Discovery and inspection
items.gist: A party may give notice to the other to produce for inspection documents referred to in his pleadings or affidavits.

items.head: Non-compliance
items.group: Order XI — Discovery and inspection
items.gist: If a party fails to comply with an order for discovery or inspection, the plaintiff's suit may be dismissed or the defendant's defence struck out.

items.head: Notice of admission of case
items.group: Order XII — Admissions
items.gist: A party may, by pleading or in writing, admit the truth of the whole or part of the other party's case.

items.head: Notice to admit documents
items.group: Order XII — Admissions
items.gist: A party may call on the other to admit documents within 15 days of service; unreasonable refusal can be visited with costs.

items.head: Notice to admit facts
items.group: Order XII — Admissions
items.gist: A party may call on the other to admit specified facts within 15 days.

items.head: Judgment on admissions
items.group: Order XII — Admissions
items.gist: Where admissions of fact are made in pleadings or otherwise, the court may at any stage pass judgment on them without waiting for other questions to be decided.

items.head: Originals to be produced
items.group: Order XIII — Production, impounding and return of documents
items.gist: Parties produce all original documents in their possession, already filed in copy, on or before settlement of issues.

items.head: Rejection of irrelevant documents
items.group: Order XIII — Production, impounding and return of documents
items.gist: The court may reject any document it considers irrelevant or otherwise inadmissible, recording the grounds.

items.head: Endorsement on admitted documents
items.group: Order XIII — Production, impounding and return of documents
items.gist: Every document admitted in evidence is endorsed with the suit number, the party producing it and the date — the 'exhibit' mark.

items.head: Impounding
items.group: Order XIII — Production, impounding and return of documents
items.gist: The court may order any document produced before it to be impounded and kept in custody.

items.head: Return of admitted documents
items.group: Order XIII — Production, impounding and return of documents
items.gist: Admitted documents are returned after the time for appeal has passed or the appeal is disposed of; earlier only on a certified copy being substituted.

items.head: Framing of issues
items.group: Order XIV — Settlement of issues
items.gist: Issues arise when a material proposition of fact or law is affirmed by one party and denied by the other. The court frames them at the first hearing after reading the pleadings and examining the parties.

items.head: Judgment on all issues; preliminary issue of law
items.group: Order XIV — Settlement of issues
items.gist: The court pronounces judgment on all issues. But where an issue of law alone (jurisdiction, or a bar created by law) can dispose of the suit, it may try that issue first.

items.head: Amending and striking out issues
items.group: Order XIV — Settlement of issues
items.gist: The court may amend issues, frame additional issues, or strike out issues wrongly framed, at any time before passing the decree.

items.head: Parties not at issue
items.group: Order XV — Disposal of the suit at the first hearing
items.gist: If at the first hearing the parties are not at issue on any question of law or fact, the court may pronounce judgment at once.

items.head: List of witnesses
items.group: Order XVI — Summoning and attendance of witnesses
items.gist: Parties present a list of witnesses, and obtain summons for them, not later than 15 days after the date on which issues are settled.

items.head: Expenses of witnesses
items.group: Order XVI — Summoning and attendance of witnesses
items.gist: The party applying for summons pays into court the sum needed for the witness's travelling and other expenses.

items.head: Witness who fails to comply
items.group: Order XVI — Summoning and attendance of witnesses
items.gist: If a summoned witness fails to attend without lawful excuse, the court may issue a proclamation, a warrant (with or without bail) and attach his property.

items.head: Court may grant time
items.group: Order XVII — Adjournments
items.gist: The court may adjourn the hearing for sufficient cause shown, and makes an order for costs. No adjournment is granted more than three times to a party during the hearing of the suit.

items.head: Parties absent on adjourned day
items.group: Order XVII — Adjournments
items.gist: If the parties fail to appear on the adjourned day, the court may dispose of the suit in one of the modes in Order IX.

items.head: Default by a party who was granted time
items.group: Order XVII — Adjournments
items.gist: If a party who was granted time fails to produce evidence or take the step required, the court may decide the suit forthwith.

items.head: Right to begin
items.group: Order XVIII — Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
items.gist: The plaintiff has the right to begin — unless the defendant admits the facts alleged and contends that on a point of law or on additional facts the plaintiff is not entitled to relief, in which case the defendant begins.

items.head: Statement and production of evidence
items.group: Order XVIII — Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
items.gist: The party beginning states his case and produces evidence; the other party then states his case and evidence. Parties may file written arguments before oral arguments close.

items.head: Recording of evidence
items.group: Order XVIII — Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
items.gist: Examination-in-chief of every witness is by affidavit. Cross-examination and re-examination may be recorded by the court or by a commissioner appointed by it.

items.head: Evidence in appealable cases
items.group: Order XVIII — Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
items.gist: In appealable cases, evidence is taken down in the language of the court, in the presence and under the superintendence of the judge.

items.head: Recalling a witness
items.group: Order XVIII — Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
items.gist: The court may at any stage recall a witness who has been examined and put such questions as it thinks fit.

items.head: Proof by affidavit
items.group: Order XIX — Affidavits
items.gist: The court may for sufficient reason order any particular fact to be proved by affidavit.

items.head: Cross-examination of deponent
items.group: Order XIX — Affidavits
items.gist: The court may order the deponent to attend for cross-examination.

items.head: Contents of affidavits
items.group: Order XIX — Affidavits
items.gist: Affidavits are confined to facts within the deponent's own knowledge — except on interlocutory applications, where statements of belief may be admitted if the grounds are stated.

items.head: Pronouncement of judgment
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: Judgment is pronounced in open court at once, or as soon as possible — ordinarily within 30 days of the end of the hearing, and not later than 60 days for exceptional reasons.

items.head: Contents of judgment
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: Judgments (other than in small cause courts) contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision on them, and the reasons.

items.head: Finding on each issue
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: The court states its finding or decision, with reasons, on each separate issue.

items.head: Contents of decree
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: The decree agrees with the judgment; it states the number of the suit, the parties, the relief granted and the costs.

items.head: Preparation of decree
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: The decree is drawn up as early as possible, ideally within 15 days of the judgment.

items.head: Decree for possession and mesne profits
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: In a suit for possession and rent or mesne profits, the decree may provide for possession, past mesne profits and an inquiry into future mesne profits.

items.head: Decree in partition suit
items.group: Order XX — Judgment and decree
items.gist: In a partition suit the court may pass a preliminary decree declaring the shares, followed by a final decree dividing the property.

items.head: Costs of particular items
items.group: Order XX-A — Costs
items.gist: Costs include expenses for notices, typing, inspection of records, producing witnesses and similar items, as the court allows.

items.head: Modes of paying money under decree
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Money payable under a decree may be paid into the executing court, out of court to the decree-holder, or as the court directs.

items.head: Application for execution
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: The decree-holder applies to the court that passed the decree (or the court to which it has been sent) for execution.

items.head: Oral and written applications
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: For a money decree, the court may order immediate execution on an oral application at the time of the decree. Otherwise the application is in writing, with the decree particulars and the mode of execution sought.

items.head: Transferee of decree
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: A person to whom a decree is transferred may apply for execution, after notice to the transferor and the judgment-debtor.

items.head: Notice to show cause
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Notice is issued to the judgment-debtor where execution is applied for more than two years after the decree, or against a legal representative.

items.head: Decree for payment of money
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: A money decree may be executed by detention of the judgment-debtor in civil prison, by attachment and sale of his property, or both.

items.head: Decree for specific performance or injunction
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Such decrees may be enforced by detention of the disobeying party in civil prison, attachment of his property, or both.

items.head: Notice before arrest
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Before ordering arrest for a money decree, the court ordinarily issues notice to the judgment-debtor to show cause why he should not be committed to civil prison.

items.head: Examination of judgment-debtor as to property
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: The decree-holder may apply for the judgment-debtor to be orally examined about his assets.

items.head: Attachment of immovable property
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Attachment is made by an order prohibiting the judgment-debtor from transferring or charging the property, proclaimed publicly.

items.head: Claims and objections to attachment
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Objections by any person to the attachment of property are decided by the executing court itself, not by a separate suit.

items.head: Power to order sale
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: The executing court may order attached property to be sold and the proceeds paid to the decree-holder.

items.head: Proclamation of sale
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Sale by public auction is preceded by a proclamation stating the time and place of sale and particulars of the property.

items.head: Deposit by purchaser
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: The purchaser of immovable property deposits 25% of the purchase money immediately on being declared the purchaser.

items.head: Payment of balance
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: The balance is paid within 15 days of the sale.

items.head: Setting aside sale on deposit
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: Any person claiming an interest may apply to set aside the sale by depositing the amount in the proclamation, less any amount received, plus 5% of the purchase money for the purchaser.

items.head: Setting aside sale for irregularity or fraud
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: A sale may be set aside for material irregularity or fraud in publishing or conducting it, if the applicant has suffered substantial injury because of it.

items.head: Sale becomes absolute
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: If no application under rr.89–91 is made or it is disallowed, the court confirms the sale and it becomes absolute.

items.head: Resistance to delivery of possession
items.group: Order XXI — Execution of decrees and orders
items.gist: If the decree-holder or purchaser is resisted or obstructed in obtaining possession, he may apply to the court, which decides all questions arising between the parties (rr.97–101).

items.head: No abatement if right to sue survives
items.group: Order XXII — Death, marriage and insolvency of parties
items.gist: A suit does not abate on the death of a party if the right to sue survives.

items.head: Death of a plaintiff
items.group: Order XXII — Death, marriage and insolvency of parties
items.gist: Legal representatives of a deceased plaintiff must be brought on record within the limitation period (90 days, Art. 120), otherwise the suit abates as to that plaintiff.

items.head: Death of a defendant
items.group: Order XXII — Death, marriage and insolvency of parties
items.gist: Legal representatives of a deceased defendant must be brought on record in time, otherwise the suit abates as against that defendant.

items.head: Effect of abatement
items.group: Order XXII — Death, marriage and insolvency of parties
items.gist: No fresh suit can be brought on the same cause of action; but an application may be made to set aside the abatement for sufficient cause.

items.head: Devolution of interest during suit
items.group: Order XXII — Death, marriage and insolvency of parties
items.gist: When an interest is assigned or devolves during the suit, the suit may continue by or against the person to whom it has passed, with the court's leave.

items.head: Withdrawal of suit
items.group: Order XXIII — Withdrawal and adjustment of suits
items.gist: The plaintiff may withdraw a suit or abandon part of a claim. With the court's permission (formal defect or other sufficient grounds) he may sue afresh; without it, a fresh suit on the same subject-matter is barred.

items.head: Compromise of suit
items.group: Order XXIII — Withdrawal and adjustment of suits
items.gist: Where the suit is adjusted by a lawful agreement or compromise in writing signed by the parties, the court records it and passes a decree accordingly.

items.head: Bar to suit
items.group: Order XXIII — Withdrawal and adjustment of suits
items.gist: No suit lies to set aside a decree on the ground that the compromise on which it is based was not lawful.

items.head: Deposit by defendant
items.group: Order XXIV — Payment into court
items.gist: In a suit for a debt or damages, the defendant may deposit into court the amount he considers a full satisfaction of the claim. Interest stops running on the deposited amount.

items.head: When security may be required
items.group: Order XXV — Security for costs
items.gist: The court may order the plaintiff to give security for the defendant's costs — for example where the plaintiff resides outside India and has no sufficient immovable property in India.

items.head: Commission to examine witnesses
items.group: Order XXVI — Commissions
items.gist: The court may issue a commission to examine a witness who is exempt from attending court or unable to attend because of sickness or infirmity.

items.head: Local investigation
items.group: Order XXVI — Commissions
items.gist: The court may issue a commission for a local investigation to clarify a matter in dispute, ascertain market value, or mesne profits.

items.head: Scientific investigation
items.group: Order XXVI — Commissions
items.gist: Where a question involves a scientific investigation that cannot conveniently be conducted before the court, a commission may be issued.

items.head: Examination of accounts
items.group: Order XXVI — Commissions
items.gist: In a suit needing examination or adjustment of accounts, the court may issue a commission to a suitable person.

items.head: Partition
items.group: Order XXVI — Commissions
items.gist: Where a preliminary decree for partition has been passed, the court may issue a commission to make the partition.

items.head: Signing of pleadings
items.group: Order XXVII — Suits by or against the Government or public officers
items.gist: In suits by or against the Government, pleadings are signed by a person the Government appoints.

items.head: Government pleader as agent
items.group: Order XXVII — Suits by or against the Government or public officers
items.gist: The Government pleader is the agent of the Government for receiving processes against it.

items.head: Government to be joined
items.group: Order XXVII — Suits by or against the Government or public officers
items.gist: Where a suit is filed against a public officer for an act done in his official capacity, the Government is joined as a party.

items.head: Court to assist settlement
items.group: Order XXVII — Suits by or against the Government or public officers
items.gist: In suits against the Government or a public officer, the court should first try to help the parties reach a settlement.

items.head: Notice to Attorney General / Advocate General
items.group: Order XXVII-A — Suits involving a question on interpretation of the Constitution
items.gist: Where a substantial question of law on the interpretation of the Constitution arises, the court gives notice to the Attorney General of India or the State's Advocate General.

items.head: Authorising another to sue or defend
items.group: Order XXVIII — Suits by or against military, naval men or airmen
items.gist: A serving officer or soldier who cannot get leave may authorise another person to sue or defend for him.

items.head: Signing and verifying pleadings
items.group: Order XXIX — Suits by or against corporations
items.gist: Pleadings of a corporation may be signed and verified by its secretary, a director or other principal officer able to depose to the facts.

items.head: Suing in the firm name
items.group: Order XXX — Suits by or against firms
items.gist: Two or more persons claiming or liable as partners may sue or be sued in the name of their firm.

items.head: Business in another name
items.group: Order XXX — Suits by or against firms
items.gist: A person carrying on business in a name other than his own may be sued in that name as if it were a firm name.

items.head: Representation of beneficiaries
items.group: Order XXXI — Suits by or against trustees, executors and administrators
items.gist: In suits concerning property vested in a trustee, executor or administrator, he represents the beneficiaries, who need not ordinarily be made parties.

items.head: Minor to sue by next friend
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: Every suit by a minor is instituted in his name by a person called his next friend.

items.head: Guardian ad litem
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: Where the defendant is a minor, the court appoints a proper person as guardian for the suit (guardian ad litem).

items.head: Who may act
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: Any person of sound mind who has attained majority may act as next friend or guardian, provided his interest is not adverse to the minor's.

items.head: Compromise needs leave
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: A next friend or guardian cannot enter into any agreement or compromise on behalf of the minor without the court's leave. A compromise without leave is voidable against the minor.

items.head: On attaining majority
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: A minor plaintiff who becomes a major elects whether to proceed with the suit or abandon it.

items.head: Persons of unsound mind
items.group: Order XXXII — Suits by or against minors and persons of unsound mind
items.gist: Rules 1 to 14 apply, as far as may be, to persons of unsound mind or who are mentally infirm.

items.head: Duty to assist settlement
items.group: Order XXXII-A — Suits relating to matters concerning the family
items.gist: In family suits, the court first tries to assist the parties in arriving at a settlement, and may hold proceedings in camera and take help from a welfare expert.

items.head: Indigent person
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: A suit may be instituted by an indigent person — one without sufficient means to pay the court-fee (property exempt from attachment and the subject-matter of the suit are left out of account).

items.head: Rejection of application
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: The application is rejected if it is not properly framed, the applicant is not indigent, he has fraudulently disposed of property, his allegations show no cause of action, or he has made an agreement giving another person an interest in the subject-matter.

items.head: Inquiry
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: The court hears evidence on the applicant's indigency, and the Government pleader and the opposite party may oppose.

items.head: Costs where indigent succeeds
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: If the indigent plaintiff succeeds, the court-fee he would have paid is recovered and is a first charge on the subject-matter of the suit.

items.head: Where indigent fails
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: If he fails, or permission to sue is withdrawn, the court orders him to pay the court-fee.

items.head: Free legal services
items.group: Order XXXIII — Suits by indigent persons
items.gist: The Government may provide free legal services to persons permitted to sue as indigent persons.

items.head: Preliminary decree in foreclosure suit
items.group: Order XXXIV — Suits relating to mortgages of immovable property
items.gist: The court passes a preliminary decree declaring the amount due and directing payment by a fixed date, failing which the mortgagor is debarred from redeeming.

items.head: Preliminary decree in suit for sale
items.group: Order XXXIV — Suits relating to mortgages of immovable property
items.gist: In a suit for sale, the court passes a preliminary decree directing that, if payment is not made, the property be sold.

items.head: Redemption suit
items.group: Order XXXIV — Suits relating to mortgages of immovable property
items.gist: In a suit for redemption, the court declares the amount due and directs reconveyance on payment.

items.head: Plaint in interpleader suit
items.group: Order XXXV — Interpleader
items.gist: The plaint states that the plaintiff claims no interest in the thing other than charges or costs, that the defendants claim it adversely, and that there is no collusion.

items.head: Payment into court
items.group: Order XXXV — Interpleader
items.gist: The court may order the thing claimed to be paid or placed in its custody.

items.head: Discharge of plaintiff
items.group: Order XXXV — Interpleader
items.gist: At the first hearing the court may discharge the plaintiff from liability, award his costs, and let the claimants fight it out.

items.head: Power to state a case
items.group: Order XXXVI — Special case
items.gist: Parties may agree to state a question of fact or law in the form of a case for the court's opinion.

items.head: Courts and classes of suits
items.group: Order XXXVII — Summary procedure
items.gist: Applies to suits on bills of exchange, hundis and promissory notes, and suits to recover a debt or liquidated sum under a written contract, enactment or guarantee (and commercial disputes).

items.head: Institution
items.group: Order XXXVII — Summary procedure
items.gist: The defendant cannot defend unless he enters appearance within 10 days of service; otherwise the plaintiff is entitled to a decree.

items.head: Leave to defend
items.group: Order XXXVII — Summary procedure
items.gist: The defendant applies for leave to defend within 10 days of the summons for judgment. Leave is refused only where the defence is frivolous or vexatious, or there is no substantial defence.

items.head: Setting aside decree
items.group: Order XXXVII — Summary procedure
items.gist: After decree the court may, in special circumstances, set it aside and give leave to appear and defend.

items.head: Arrest before judgment
items.group: Order XXXVIII — Arrest and attachment before judgment
items.gist: If the defendant, with intent to delay the plaintiff or avoid the court's process, is about to abscond or leave its jurisdiction, the court may require him to furnish security for his appearance.

items.head: Attachment before judgment
items.group: Order XXXVIII — Arrest and attachment before judgment
items.gist: If the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay execution of a decree, is about to dispose of or remove his property, the court may direct him to furnish security or attach the property.

items.head: Withdrawal of attachment
items.group: Order XXXVIII — Arrest and attachment before judgment
items.gist: An attachment before judgment is withdrawn when security is furnished or the suit is dismissed.

items.head: Rights of strangers
items.group: Order XXXVIII — Arrest and attachment before judgment
items.gist: Attachment before judgment does not affect the rights of persons not party to the suit.

items.head: Cases for temporary injunction
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: A temporary injunction may be granted where property in dispute is in danger of being wasted, damaged or alienated; the defendant threatens to dispose of property to defraud creditors; or threatens to dispossess or injure the plaintiff.

items.head: Injunction to restrain repetition of breach
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: In a suit to restrain breach of contract or other injury, the plaintiff may seek a temporary injunction against the breach or injury complained of.

items.head: Consequence of disobedience
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: Disobedience or breach of an injunction may be punished by attachment of property and detention in civil prison for up to three months.

items.head: Notice before injunction
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: Before granting an injunction the court gives notice to the opposite party — unless the object would be defeated by delay, in which case it records reasons for an ex parte injunction.

items.head: Decide within 30 days
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: Where an ex parte injunction is granted, the court tries to finally dispose of the application within 30 days.

items.head: Vary or set aside
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: An order for injunction may be discharged, varied or set aside on application by a dissatisfied party.

items.head: Detention, preservation, inspection
items.group: Order XXXIX — Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
items.gist: The court may order detention, preservation or inspection of any property that is the subject-matter of the suit.

items.head: Appointment
items.group: Order XL — Appointment of receivers
items.gist: Where it appears just and convenient, the court may appoint a receiver of any property, remove anyone from its possession or custody, and give the receiver powers to manage, collect rents and profits.

items.head: Duties
items.group: Order XL — Appointment of receivers
items.gist: A receiver furnishes security, submits accounts as directed, pays the amounts due from him, and is responsible for loss caused by his wilful default or gross negligence.

items.head: Memorandum of appeal
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: An appeal is preferred by a memorandum signed by the appellant or his pleader, with a copy of the judgment, setting out the grounds of objection concisely.

items.head: Delay application
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: An appeal filed after the limitation period must be accompanied by an application for condonation of delay.

items.head: Stay by appellate court
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: An appeal does not operate as a stay. The court may order stay if substantial loss may result, the application is made without unreasonable delay, and security is given.

items.head: Dismissal without notice
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: The appellate court may dismiss the appeal after hearing the appellant, without sending notice to the respondent.

items.head: Cross-objection
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: A respondent who has not appealed may file a cross-objection to the decree within one month of service of notice of the appeal.

items.head: Remand
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: Where the trial court decided the suit on a preliminary point and the decree is reversed, the appellate court may remand the case for trial.

items.head: Remand in other cases
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: Where the decree is reversed and a retrial is necessary, the appellate court may also remand.

items.head: Final decision where evidence sufficient
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: Where the evidence on record is sufficient, the appellate court may finally decide the case.

items.head: Additional evidence
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: Parties cannot produce new evidence in appeal, except where the trial court wrongly refused it, the party could not produce it despite due diligence, or the appellate court requires it.

items.head: Contents of appellate judgment
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: The judgment states the points for determination, the decision on them, the reasons, and the relief to which the appellant is entitled where the decree is reversed or varied.

items.head: Power of appellate court
items.group: Order XLI — Appeals from original decrees
items.gist: The appellate court may pass any decree that ought to have been passed, even in favour of parties who have not appealed.

items.head: Procedure
items.group: Order XLII — Appeals from appellate decrees
items.gist: Rules of Order XLI apply, as far as may be, to second appeals.

items.head: Substantial question of law
items.group: Order XLII — Appeals from appellate decrees
items.gist: When admitting a second appeal, the court formulates the substantial question of law to be argued.

items.head: Appealable orders
items.group: Order XLIII — Appeals from orders
items.gist: An appeal lies from orders listed here — e.g. returning a plaint (O.VII r.10), refusing to restore a suit (O.IX r.9), refusing to set aside an ex parte decree (O.IX r.13), injunction orders (O.XXXIX rr.1, 2, 2A, 4, 10) and receiver orders (O.XL r.1).

items.head: Challenge to compromise in decree appeal
items.group: Order XLIII — Appeals from orders
items.gist: In an appeal against a decree, a party may contend that a compromise ought or ought not to have been recorded.

items.head: Who may appeal as indigent
items.group: Order XLIV — Appeals by indigent persons
items.gist: A person unable to pay the fee for the memorandum of appeal may apply to appeal as an indigent person.

items.head: Certificate
items.group: Order XLV — Appeals to the Supreme Court
items.gist: An appeal to the Supreme Court requires a certificate from the High Court that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance that needs to be decided by the Supreme Court.

items.head: Reference to the High Court
items.group: Order XLVI — Reference
items.gist: Where a case raises a question of law on which the court entertains reasonable doubt — such as the validity of an Act — it may state a case and refer it to the High Court (S.113).

items.head: Application for review
items.group: Order XLVII — Review
items.gist: Review lies on discovery of new and important matter or evidence not available despite due diligence, a mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason.

items.head: Order rejecting review not appealable
items.group: Order XLVII — Review
items.gist: An order rejecting a review application is not appealable; an order granting it may be objected to.

items.head: No second review
items.group: Order XLVII — Review
items.gist: No application to review an order made on a review application, or a decree passed on review, is entertained.

items.head: Process served at party's cost
items.group: Order XLVIII — Miscellaneous
items.gist: Every process is served at the cost of the party issuing it, unless the court directs otherwise.

items.head: Exemptions
items.group: Order XLIX — Chartered High Courts
items.gist: Certain rules of the First Schedule do not apply to chartered High Courts exercising original civil jurisdiction.

items.head: Provisions not applicable
items.group: Order L — Provincial Small Cause Courts
items.gist: Specified provisions of the Code do not apply to Provincial Small Cause Courts.

items.head: Application
items.group: Order LI — Presidency Small Cause Courts
items.gist: Specified provisions of the Code apply to Presidency Small Cause Courts.
